draft.title: Change over time
card: Places and environments are always changing. Geographers study change over time to see what a place was like, how it is now and how it may be later.
Change happens over different time spans. A flood can reshape a river bank in a day. A coastline can erode over years. Climate can shift over centuries.
Some changes are natural, such as a bushfire or a volcanic eruption. Others come from people, such as clearing land for farms or building a new suburb.
The time span chosen can change what a geographer sees. A short span may show a sudden event. A long span may show a slow trend that is easy to miss.
draft.remember: Change can be fast or slow, so the time span a geographer looks at shapes what they find.

a.q: Why do geographers study a place over different time spans?
opts: Short and long spans can show different kinds of change
Only long spans can show that a place has changed
Natural change is slow and human change is always fast
Time spans matter only for events caused by people
a.why: A short span can show a sudden event such as a flood, while a long span can show a slow trend such as climate change. It is wrong to say only long spans show change, because a flood shows big change in a day.
a.clue: Think about what a flood and a slow climate shift each look like.

b.q: Over 40 years, a seaside town in NSW has lost a little beach sand each year. A storm last week removed a large strip in one night. Which statement fits this case?
opts: Both a slow trend and a sudden event are changing the beach
Only the storm matters, because it caused the biggest change
Only the 40 year trend is change, as the storm was brief
The storm shows that the beach is not changing slowly
b.why: The yearly loss is a slow change over decades and the storm is a sudden change in one night. Both are change over time on different spans. Saying only the storm counts ignores the slow trend that a short span would miss.
b.clue: Can a place change slowly and suddenly at the same time?

a.best: Short and long spans can show different kinds of change

b.best: Both a slow trend and a sudden event are changing the beach

problems.detail: Three of the four options use absolutes ('always', 'Only', 'only'), while the card speaks of what spans 'may' show. The right option is the only one without an absolute, so a student can pick it without knowing the idea.
Two distractors start with 'Only', which the card never supports. This makes them easy to rule out without understanding change over different time spans.
The clue 'Can a place change slowly and suddenly at the same time?' all but states the right option, which says both a slow trend and a sudden event are changing the beach.
